title: Check if String Is Decomposable Into Value-Equal Substrings
summary: Determine if a digit string can be divided into value-equal substrings, with exactly one substring of length 2 and the rest of length 3, where a value-equal string consists of identical characters.
statement: Determine if a digit string can be divided into value-equal substrings, with exactly one substring of length 2 and the rest of length 3, where a value-equal string consists of identical characters.
constraints: Partition equal consecutive digits into groups of length three, except exactly one group of length two.
No group may mix different digits, and the entire string must be used.
hints: Only maximal runs of one digit matter because groups cannot cross a digit change.
Inspect each run length modulo three: remainder one is impossible; remainder two contributes the unique pair.
Scan runs, reject remainder one, count remainder-two runs, and accept exactly one.
A run of length 3q uses triples; length 3q+2 uses triples plus one pair; length 3q+1 cannot be partitioned. Exactly one pair completes the global rule.
editorial: A run of length 3q uses triples; length 3q+2 uses triples plus one pair; length 3q+1 cannot be partitioned. Exactly one pair completes the global rule.

tests.explanation: All three runs have length three, so the required single length-two group is missing.
The runs split as 000, 111+11, and 22, which creates two length-two groups and is invalid.
